editorial:
Imagine being a soft-hearted poet who loves bicycles and hates violence, only to be dumped in the middle of the Wild West because your dad wanted you to be a real man. That is exactly what happens to Joe. You get to watch this fish-out-of-water story unfold as Joe tries to survive in a world where everyone carries a gun. He is surrounded by three rough teachers who are basically criminals trying to toughen him up. The vibe is lighthearted and funny, making it feel more like a slapstick comedy than a serious cowboy movie. It is a great ride if you enjoy seeing a gentle soul try to find his way in a rough neighborhood.

The acting is great, especially the way Joe stays true to his dreamy personality while everything goes crazy around him. While the pacing slows down a bit in the middle, the action picks up once the jealous gunman Morton enters the picture. You will love the funny clashes between Joe's polite nature and the gritty Western setting.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when Joe finally stands up to Morton. Despite his hatred for guns, Joe uses his wits and a bit of unexpected courage to defeat the villain. He proves that being a real man is not about how many people you kill, but about protecting the people you love. Joe wins over the rancher's daughter and finds a balance between his poetic side and his new toughness, bringing a happy end to his journey.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves funny westerns and underdog stories.
